articles.title: Nate Sheppard proves point after Stanford's boast on stopping the run
articles.summary: Duke RB Nate Sheppard quieted the talk of Stanford CB Brandon Nicholson with another Heisman-worthy game.
articles.body:
Nate Sheppard has seen the Heisman hype and said he's taking it with "so much grain of salt" this early in the season.

The Duke running back also saw the clip of Stanford cornerback Brandon Nicholson saying no one runs on the Cardinals' defense. The Blue Devils ' offensive line and Sheppard himself proved that wrong on Saturday, and after the 35-7 victory in which he put up 154 rushing yards and three total touchdowns, Sheppard was asked about the clip.

Yeah, so I saw the quote, I think on Wednesday, and then we actually saw the video, I think it was yesterday, on Friday, and it was the type of arrogance he had when he said it, and I think it rubbed the whole offense the wrong way," he said. "We were out there to prove a point."

Prove a point indeed, as the Blue Devils racked up 268 yards on the ground, led by their star running back, who leads the nation in all-purpose and rushing yards after Week 3. He came out strong from the start, eclipsing the 100-yard mark in the second quarter, including a 32-yard touchdown run that showcased his agility and speed and got the team on the board.

It's not exactly Sheppard's personality to look for a challenge. Still, he's already been given plenty this season, including being left off the Doak Walker Award Watch List for best running back in the country. The Louisiana native responded with a meme on Twitter and, to make sure voters were paying attention, was named Doak Walker Award Running Back of the Week after a 227-yard, two-touchdown performance against Tulane.

"I'm not looking for it, but if they're going to give it to me, I'm going to take it and run," Sheppard said.

articles.title: Rock Falls volleyball takes third at Bradley Bourbonnais: Saturday’s Sauk Valley Sports Roundup
articles.summary: Volleyball Rock Falls takes third at Bradley Bourbonnais Invite: The Rockets went 2-1 with wins over Beecher and Herscher, losing to Montini. Miley Bickett h...
articles.body:
Rock Falls takes third at Bradley Bourbonnais Invite: The Rockets went 2-1 with wins over Beecher and Herscher, losing to Montini. Miley Bickett had 51 assists and seven aces, Alivia Heald had 13 kills and three aces, Kaltrina Lecaj had 26 kills, Isela Valdivia had 30 digs and Taylor Segneri had 19 kills.

Steamers go 2-3 in Clinton: Fulton beat Clinton 25-19, 25-18 and 21-16, 23-25, 15-12. The Steamers lost to Wilton (21-12, 16-21, 15-8), Jefferson (21-12, 21-16) and Western Dubuque (20-22, 25-23, 15-12).

Kerby Germann (30 digs) led Fulton with 42 kills and Chloe Wilkin had 27. Brianna Brennan had 54 assists and Averi Bush had 39 digs. Iris Williams had six blocks.

Clinton 146, Morrison 89: Molly Brackemyer, Sarah Prombo, Lucy Bohm and Shay Steele won the 200 medley relay. Brackemyer also won the 200 freestyle, Bohm won the 50 free and 100 backstroke, and Prombo won the 100 breast.

Isaiah Rojop leads Sterling at Geneseo: Rojop took seventh in 17:42 in the 3-mile senior race.

Sterling's Lillian Hauck wins at Geneseo: Hauck took first in 21:52 in the 3-mile juniors race. Dixon's Jade Setchell was fourth in 22:21. Sterling's Sophia Davis took first among sophomores in 20:32. In the freshmen race, Dixon's Brynleigh Davis (19:58), Audrina Setchell and Grace Conderman took the top three spots.

Forreston 40, Eastland-Pearl City 20: Forreston's Connor Politsch ran for 147 yards and two scores. EPC's Deaken Hofmaster had two rushing scores.

Milledgeville 57, AFC 0: Kyson Francis had three rushing TDs and 98 yards in the win. He also threw for 73 yards.
authors: Drake Lansman, Daily Gazette, Sterling, Ill.

articles.title: Liverpool can solve one of their main problems with £80m star
articles.summary: Liverpool may have spent more than £600 million over the last couple of seasons but, they still have a few glaring issues among their ranks that need to be s...
articles.body:
Liverpool may have spent more than £600 million over the last couple of seasons but, they still have a few glaring issues among their ranks that need to be solved.

Some problems that they had at the end of the 2025-26 season have obviously been ironed out and fixed but others are going to take a bit more time.

We're also still very early in the season so, once players get fully used to Andoni Iraola's style of play and what he expects from them, things will probably run much smoother.

However, until then, the transfer market could end up being the Reds' best friend or even their worst enemy.

But, thanks to a fresh report that has just emerged, it now seems like £80 million could help them solve one of their main issues.

Crystal Palace would let Adam Wharton exit Selhurst Park for £80 million

Everyone knows that Liverpool's midfield is their weakest area at the moment.

Indeed, they haven't managed to replace Mohamed Salah yet but, with Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola being added to Andoni Iraola's ranks, Liverpool seem to have enough firepower to fill the void he left behind.

Of course, they'd be much better off if they actually managed to bring a natural right-winger in but, after the fees they were being quoted for Ismaila Sarr and Yankuba Minteh, it's not hard to understand why a right-winger wasn't signed.

So, despite Liverpool's attack still needing reinforcement, their midfielders are their main issues.

At the moment, Alexis Mac Allister is their best central midfielder by a country mile with his ability to defend and attack allowing him to become key in Iraola's system.

But, since the Reds still need to shore up their midfield ranks a bit more, the fact that Crystal Palace would be willing to sell Adam Wharton for £80 million will be music to their ears.

"Wharton looks set to be available for a fee in the region of £80m this January, according to some sources," Caught Offside wrote .

"It will be interesting to see what CFC do, but there is an increased urgency to strengthen in the middle of the park, even if there hasn't previously been unanimous backing for Wharton.

"The 22-year-old has also been on the radar of Liverpool."

£80 million is all Liverpool will need to spend to fix their main issue

The Englishman has become one of Palace's most important players over the last few years and, since Elliott Anderson joined Manchester City for £116 million this summer, the £80 million that Pierre Sage wants for Wharton is justified.

His range of passing and ability to stay back and defend are likely two of the key reasons why Liverpool want him.

The fact that he's homegrown is also a massive help as, at the moment, the Reds have managed to fill all of their foreign places in their squad.

Wharton is also only 22 years old so, even though he's already at the top of his game, there's plenty of time for him to grow into an even better player than he already is.

£80 million may seem quite steep but, if it helps solidify Liverpool's ranks and ensures that they can start challenging for silverware again, the Englishman would be worth every penny.

articles.title: Jets, Packers tied 7-7 at halftime
articles.summary: The Jets and Packers have not produced many offensive highlights through 30 minutes of play at a wet MetLife Stadium.
articles.body:
The Jets and Packers have not produced many offensive highlights through 30 minutes of play at a wet MetLife Stadium.

Neither team scored or moved the ball past midfield in the first quarter of the game, but they both found enough footing to post touchdowns in the second quarter. A Packers punt gave the Jets one more chance to put points on the board, but the clock ran out on the half with the Jets near midfield and the score tied 7-7.

The Packers score came on a screen pass to running back MarShawn Lloyd and the Jets answered with a six-yard run by Braelon Allen on the ensuing drive. Packers quarterback Jordan Love is 7-of-12 for 47 yards while Geno Smith is 14-of-23 for 102 yards.

The Packers lost wide receiver Jayden Reed and right tackle Zach Beko-Bewele to injuries on their first possession. Both players have been ruled out for the rest of the game and could be out longer after being carted off the field.

Neither team has turned the ball over thus far and a change on that front could help swing the result in New Jersey.

articles.title: Broncos vs. Jaguars gameday inactives for Week 2
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos are a bit banged up after a blowout loss last week with both wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. and running back RJ Harvey ruled out for this g...
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos are a bit banged up after a blowout loss last week with both wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. and running back RJ Harvey ruled out for this game and both are inactive. Not ideal entering a must-win situation at home against a strong Jacksonville Jaguars team.

With Mims out, Lil'Jordan Humphrey will be active as will Tyler Badie . You have to figure rookie Jonah Coleman will be more heavily involved today as well. With Denver down two big offensive contributors, the young guys will have to step it up.

articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase makes a poster catch to give Bengals 7-3 halftime lead
articles.summary: Ja'Marr Chase has a habit of starting slowly in Week 1 and blowing up in Week 2.
articles.body:
Ja'Marr Chase has a habit of starting slowly in Week 1 and blowing up in Week 2. He had two catches for 12 yards last week in the season opener.

The Bengals receiver made one of the best catches you will ever see with 3:29 left until halftime Sunday. His 32-yard touchdown, despite tight coverage from Derek Stingley , brought back memories of Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham 's catch over Cowboys cornerback Brandon Carr in 2014.

Chase has four catches for 48 yards, and the Bengals lead the Texans 7-3 at halftime in a defensive battle.

The Texans have outgained the Bengals 208 to 156, with three sacks of Joe Burrow . But Houston is 0-for-3 in the red zone, with drives ending at the Cincinnati 16, 18 and 19.

The Texans twice turned it over on downs, including once when holder Kai Kroeger dropped a snap on a chip-shot field goal from the 16-yard line. Kicker Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked a 37-yard field goal with 1:17 remaining in the half.

The Bengals were called for a false start on Dalton Risner on a 58-yard field goal that Evan McPherson made and decided to punt.

Burrow is 12-of-19 for 129 yards and a touchdown, and Tee Higgins has caught four for 72. Chase Brown has seven carries for 42 yards.

Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud has completed 15 of 24 passes for 182 yards. Tight end Dalton Schultz has four catches for 68 yards. David Montgomery has only 10 yards on six carries.
